title: Standard case with UPPER and LOWER
summary: Make store codes consistent with UPPER and LOWER and learn when letter case does and does not matter.

blocks.text: Store codes reach the merchandising team from several systems, and people type them in different ways: nbo-01, Nbo-01 and NBO-01 all mean the Nairobi store. Reports are easier to read, and exports easier to join, when every code looks the same.
UPPER and LOWER change the letter case of text. In this mission you will standardise store codes and look up the region of each store.

items: Objective: standardise letter case with UPPER and LOWER.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: UPPER returns the text with every letter in capitals. LOWER returns it with every letter in small letters. Digits, hyphens and spaces stay as they are.

blocks.caption: UPPER and LOWER on store codes

blocks.text: Put the typed code into capitals, then look it up in the store list. You can also keep the clean code in its own column and look that up.

items: Inside Excel, = and XLOOKUP ignore case: ="NBO-01"="nbo-01" is TRUE. So case rarely stops a lookup inside the sheet.
Standardise anyway. Some other tools, for example Power Query merges, treat NBO-01 and nbo-01 as different text, and a report with mixed case looks careless.
UPPER and LOWER do not change the length of the text, so LEN(UPPER(A2)) is the same as LEN(A2).
Tip: choose one standard (capitals for codes is common) and apply it to the whole column before you share the data.

blocks.text: Type numbers without commas or spaces, for example 12.

items: UPPER(text) gives capitals; LOWER(text) gives small letters.
Digits, hyphens and spaces are not changed, and the length stays the same.
Excel comparisons and XLOOKUP ignore case, but other tools may not.
Standardise codes in one column, then use that column for lookups and exports.

blocks.text: One standard case across the whole data set saves arguments later.

items.prompt: Excel ignores case in comparisons and lookups. Why should you still standardise the case of codes?

options.label: Other tools, such as Power Query merges, can treat NBO-01 and nbo-01 as different, and consistent codes read better
Because Excel formulas cannot compare lower-case text
Because UPPER makes the codes shorter
Because XLOOKUP only works on capitals
